gaps: P2: only a Merian interior of the 1653 royal election (#10); P5: only aerials of bombing raids on the Messerschmitt works
notes: #4 (and #2, #6, #8) is the Hoefnagel plate: Commons dates #2 to 1575, but 1575 is the renovation date carved on the wayside shrine in the corner; the cartouche says Jacob Hoefnagel drew it at the 1594 Diet, so it is from vol. 5 (1598). The 1572 six-town plate (#3, #5, #7, #9) has only a small Regensburg panel. #21 is the same photochrom as #18. P3 alternative: Turner’s 1840 watercolor #16, in color but vague. #23 (Obernetter collotype, spires finished, so after 1869) carries only a 1856–87 range; #22 stereo (1860s) is distant and dim. P6: twilight panoramas #31/#34/#35 (2006) are very wide strips.
